questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Grades under 7, so limited options.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: physical Orientation was limited upon arrival, but there was some info online

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was 1 hour of physical orientation, and some help from a student organization with what to do

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was almost nothing planned during orientation week. This made it hard to meet fellow exchange students, especially for me as I didn't live in the dorms. It was a bit uncomfortable not having a fixed schedule the first week before classes, as it made it hard to meet people in a new country

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived at Weave Living, which wasn't hard to find. It was quite expensive though, but I think it would be possible to find cheaper options if you search a little

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Can be hard to meet other exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The campus dorms are situated very far away from campus (45 min) and even further away from the city center (1-1,5 hrs)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You prioritize the courses  you want before arrival, but you can change courses during the first 2 weeks

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had some pretty thorough info online

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some classes can get filled quickly, so look into what classes you want beforehand so you can choose them quickly

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most courses were beginners courses. The academic level varied a lot between courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It varied a lot. Many of the courses had interactive teaching style, involving the students a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Gender, culture & Diversity
- Food. Science, Culture & Society
- Engineering your health
- Mandarin for non-chinese speakers
- World Religions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Gender, culture & Diversity was very intersting. The teachers were good, and it was interesting to learn about these subjects from a non-western perspective. They also had some cool guest-speakers

questions.answer: Not sure

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is quite expensive. Eating out is generally a little cheaper than in DK, but most groceries are more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most clubs were for people either playing instruments or sports at a higher level. For others, there weren't a lot of options

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There were some activities for exchange students once in a while arranged by students which were quite fun

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, going to the beach, going out in LKF (Lan Kwai Fong, party area), sightseeing, going to street markets around Mong Kok, visiting the surrounding islands

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, as HK is very international and welcoming to people of other cultures generally. The culture is generally more "western" than mainland China, so its not as big of a culture shock

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socializing with local students was generally quite difficult. They are mostly shy and keep to themselves.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The fact that the local students are so shy. They mostly didn't participate orally in class, so it was hard to have class discussions. 

Also, it was a common problem that the students were talking loudly during class, and doing a lot of other stuff (playing games on the computer etc). It was the same in all my courses. It was hard to concentrate, and seemed disrespectful towards the professor.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: HK culture is a very cool blend between modern and traditional. On the same street you can encounter a buddhist temple, a skyscraper, a fortune teller, a Lamborghini and a 100+ year old tram

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Save up enough money. Things are pretty expensive in general + a lot of students do traveling to neighboring countries, so have enough money if u don't want to miss out
- Choose  a social accommodation, if you choose not to live in the student dorm. It can be hard finding a social network otherwise, since CityU doesn't have the best facilities to meet other exchange students

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to China if you have the chance. Shenzhen (China) is only 45 min away in train, but its so different from HK. There is so many things to do here, food is cheaper (and better in my opinion) than HK, you can shop a lot of cheap tech in HaqiangBei street. Would definitely recommend

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning about HK culture and history.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some cultural differences

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
